metaDescription: Six 5000 BTU air conditioners for small RVs, vans, tents and camper bedrooms compared on window versus portable, efficiency, noise and 120V draw.
expertTake: The RecPro CL is the pick for most small campers because it is sold for RV windows and lists a CEER of 11.0. The Midea EasyCool is the value pick for a plain window unit with a remote. Skip these for a full-size trailer, where a 13,500 BTU rooftop unit is the correct tool and a 5,000 BTU unit cannot keep up.
introParagraphs: A small air conditioner has a specific place in the RV world. It cools a van, a pop-up, a small camper or a bedroom slide where a roof unit is overkill or impossible, and it plugs into an ordinary 120 volt outlet at a campground or off a generator.

Most of these are window units or portables with a hose, and the details that matter are different from a rooftop unit: window fit, efficiency, noise, where the heat goes and how much power the compressor pulls. This guide compares both styles.

products.name: RecPro CL 5,000 BTU RV Window Air Conditioner
products.description:
The RecPro CL is a window air conditioner sold for RV use, with a CEER of 11.0, a measure of cooling per watt that includes standby losses. That is an efficient number for the size and means less strain on a campground circuit or a generator. It runs on 115 volts and comes with a remote.

The window fit is the practical detail: it suits openings from 23 to 36 inches wide and needs only a 13 inch height. That fits many camper windows and van sliders, but you should measure yours before ordering. A window unit sheds heat outside through the back, so it needs an opening that can be sealed around it.

It sits in the middle price tier. Compared with the GE and Midea, it costs more for the RV positioning and efficiency figure. Seal gaps with foam or panels, and support the weight from outside if the frame is weak. In year three the wear items are the filter, the fan motor and the window seal, and a monthly filter wash is the best prevention. Keep a spare set of foam seals in the cabinet.
products.bestFor: Small campers and vans with a window that can host a unit.

products.name: Midea EasyCool 5,000 BTU Window Air Conditioner
products.description:
The Midea EasyCool is a residential window unit that works well in a small camper if the window fits. It lists a 52 dB low mode, three modes and an LED display with remote. All mounting accessories are in the box.

The listing says it cools up to 150 square feet, which is a good guide to the maximum space for a 5,000 BTU unit. A van or a small camper is far below that, so it will cool quickly. It sits in the lower price tier.

Compared with the RecPro, it is a home product, not an RV one, and it does not list a CEER in the features. Check the window width and the plug before buying. Because it is a residential unit, the plug and cord are made for a house outlet, so avoid extension cords and use a short, heavy cord if you must. Brace the unit from outside if the window frame is thin.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who need a plain window unit with a remote.
cons: No CEER stated in the features

products.name: GE 5,000 BTU Digital Window Air Conditioner
products.description:
GE's digital window unit has a thermostat with a 64F to 86F range, an LED display and a remote. The energy saver mode auto-cycles the compressor to hold the set temperature while using less power. Precise temperature control matters in a small space where a few degrees feels large.

The cycling compressor is not the same as an inverter that ramps its speed, but it avoids running flat out when the setpoint is met. It sits in the lower-middle price tier. A major brand means filters and parts are easy to find.

Compared with the Midea, it adds digital precision and a brand name. Check the window fit and the power cord reach. The eco mode is useful overnight, when the compressor cycles off and the fan idles, which lowers noise. Keep the remote in a drawer or use the panel so it does not go missing on a trip.
products.bestFor: Campers that want a digital thermostat and a major brand.

products.name: Frigidaire 5,000 BTU Window-Mounted Air Conditioner
products.description:
Frigidaire's window unit offers customizable temperature settings, two fan speeds and an easy-to-clean washable filter. The filter is the practical feature, because a clogged filter is the most common reason a small air conditioner freezes up. The listing quotes 52 dBA, suited to a bedroom.

It cools up to 150 square feet, plenty for a van or a small camper. It sits in the lower-middle price tier. Compared with the GE, it has a simpler control set.

Wash the filter monthly in dusty camps. Keep the back of the unit clear of obstructions so hot air can leave. Rinse the filter with lukewarm water and let it dry fully before it goes back in. A damp filter can smell musty after a few days of use.
products.bestFor: Campers where filter cleaning will be frequent.
pros: Washable filter is easy to reach
cons: Simpler controls than the digital GE

products.name: SXQYCH 5000 BTU 110V Portable Camping Air Conditioner

specList.label: Modes
specList.value: Cool, heat, fan, dehumidify, circulate, sleep

products.description:
This portable camping unit lists a 490 watt draw, which is about 4 amps at 120 volts, a modest load for a campground outlet or a generator. It combines cooling, heating, fan, dehumidifier, air circulation and sleep modes in one compact body. It is pitched at tents, RVs and small spaces.

A portable needs a hose to the outside for the hot exhaust, so the placement has to leave room for that. The 490 watt figure is low enough to run beside other loads on a 30 amp service. It sits in the middle price tier.

Compared with the window units, it needs no window frame but is usually louder and less efficient. Route the hose carefully so hot air does not return. Pay attention to the exhaust hose length and keep it short and straight, because every bend and foot of hose reduces the air it can move. Insulate the hose if it passes through a sunny spot.
products.bestFor: Tents and campers without a suitable window frame.
pros: 490 watt draw is easy on generators
cons: Less efficient than a good window unit

products.name: Countrymod 5000 BTU Portable Camping Air Conditioner
products.description:
Countrymod lists a sleep mode as low as 45 dB, an adjustable air outlet and four modes. The adjustable outlet lets you aim cool air at a bed, which is smart in a camper because directed air feels cooler than diffuse air. It runs on standard 110 volt power.

A 45 dB claim is a best case for sleep mode on the lowest setting. It sits in the lower-middle price tier. Compared with the SXQYCH, it lists a noise figure and an aimable outlet but no heating mode.

Vent the hose outside and elevate the unit if the floor is damp. Point the aimable outlet at the bed or the seat rather than at a wall so the airflow does the most good. Drain any condensate before storage to avoid mildew.
products.bestFor: Campers who want a quiet portable with an aimable outlet.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 5,000 BTU unit cools up to about 150 square feet in a house. A van or a small camper is far smaller, but poor insulation and sun load can eat that capacity. A full-size trailer needs a 13,500 BTU rooftop unit instead. A rule of thumb is to keep the sun out first, because shades, reflective window covers and shade parking often cut the load more cheaply than extra cooling capacity.

Window units like the RecPro, GE, Midea and Frigidaire reject heat through the back and are efficient. Portables like SXQYCH and Countrymod need a hose to the outside and are usually less efficient. Choose by what your rig has. If you will run it from a generator, check the starting surge on the nameplate and size the generator with margin above it.

RecPro lists a CEER of 11.0. Higher CEER means more cooling per watt, which matters on a generator or a 30 amp circuit. For others, check the nameplate watts. Choose a window unit if you can host one, because it is more efficient and quieter than a portable with a hose.

SXQYCH lists 490 watts, about 4 amps at 120 volts. A window unit draws several hundred watts too. A compressor starts with a surge, so a generator with margin helps. Measure the window height and width and the depth of the sill, because a unit that hangs unsupported can stress a thin camper frame.

RecPro fits 23 to 36 inches wide and 13 inches high. Measure the opening and plan to seal the gaps with foam. A poor seal lets hot air back in and wastes the capacity. Seal the gaps around the unit with foam or panels, because leaks waste cooling and let in insects.

Frigidaire quotes 52 dBA, Midea 52 dB and Countrymod 45 dB in sleep mode. Every 10 dB sounds about twice as loud, so a quiet figure matters for sleeping. For battery-only use, consider a DC air conditioner instead, because running a 120V unit through an inverter wastes a lot of battery power. Plan where the condensate drains, because a window unit sheds water outside and a portable may need emptying.

specDecoder.meaning: Cooling capacity per hour. It does not account for sun or insulation.
Combined energy efficiency ratio, cooling per watt including standby. Higher is better, and it includes standby draw.
Power draw. Divide by 120 for amps. It is the number that decides the generator size.
Sound level at a set distance. A quiet claim usually describes the lowest speed.
specDecoder.watchFor: Countrymod lists 45 dB in sleep mode.

specDecoder.meaning: The room size the BTU rating can cool in a house. Treat it as a house-room guide, not a camper rating.

cards.text: A window that fits, a seal and a circuit that can handle the compressor surge.

maintenance.why: A clogged filter freezes the coil. Do it with the unit off and the filter fully dry before reinstalling.
Dust cuts efficiency. Use a soft brush and vacuum, with the power off.
Gaps let hot air back in. Look for light at the edges and for cracked foam.
Standing water grows mold. Tilt the unit gently to empty the pan.
A warm plug signals a poor connection. Replace a cord that feels stiff or warm.

faq.q: Is 5,000 BTU enough for an RV?
faq.a: For a van or a small camper, yes. For a full-size trailer, no. For a van or small camper, the capacity is usually fine if the sun load is controlled.

faq.q: How much does a 5,000 BTU air conditioner cost?
faq.a: Prices range from a lower tier to a middle tier. Check the listing. Prices change, so compare tiers and what is included, such as a remote, mounting kit and filter.

faq.q: Can I run it on a generator?
faq.a: Yes if the generator has margin for the starting surge. Check the nameplate. Check the nameplate watts and the generator size, because the starting surge is higher than the running draw.
Window units are more efficient. Portables suit tents and rigs without a window. A window unit is more efficient, but a portable fits where there is no window.

faq.q: Can it run on a battery?
faq.a: Not practically through an inverter. For battery power, a DC air conditioner is better. An inverter wastes a large share of battery power, so rely on shore power or a generator for these units.

Many last several seasons with clean filters and coils. Clean filters and coils are the best way to extend life. Cooling off a camper before you load it, rather than after, makes any small unit feel stronger.
